checks.dec114_def4: IsLine.diff_eq_halfLines: for E a finite-dimensional real Hausdorff TVS, a line D (IsLine D: s(L − {O}) with finrank L = 2) and m ∈ D, there are independent v, w with m = s(v), D = s(span{v, w} − {O}), D \ {m, −m} = halfLine v w ∪ halfLine v (−w), the two half-lines disjoint and each connected (hence nonempty), and D \ {m, −m} not preconnected: so the two half-lines are exactly its components. This is all of « Deux points diamétralement opposés divisent une droite en deux demi-droites ». The decomposition, disjointness and connectedness hold in any real TVS (no finite dimension). Only the not-connected clause takes a continuous separating form outside finite dimension (not_isPreconnected_linearSubvariety_pair_diff), and the printed sentence does not assert it. The finite-dimensional packaging is the same convention DEC-114 adopted for Déf. 3. The other Exemples (two opposite points: linearSubvariety_span_singleton, mk_ne_neg_mk; droite: IsLine; hyperplan, S(T) [sic] read S(E): IsHyperplane) are as in round 1. Instantiated at S n in a scratch file
checks.dec114_def5: isOpenHemisphere_frontier_closure: H open, F H = l⁻¹(Ioi 0), l ≠ 0 ⟹ h := s(ker l − {O}) is a hyperplane, closed, F(h) ∪ {0} = l⁻¹{0}, frontier H = h, closure H = H ∪ h. No continuity assumed, as the docstring says. closedHyperplane_converse: IsHyperplane h ∧ IsClosed h ⟹ ∃ l : E →L[ℝ] ℝ, l ≠ 0, F h ∪ {0} = l⁻¹{0}, hᶜ = H_l ∪ H_{−l}, disjoint, both IsOpenHemisphere, both of frontier h. Together with openHemisphere_eq_iff (positive multiplier), hyperplane_eq_iff (nonzero multiplier) and continuous_of_F_union_eq, every printed assertion of l.202–220 is proved under the l ≠ 0 reading. The reading is worded as a reading, and isOpenHemisphere_empty and frontier_openHemisphere_zero are kept as 'Remark (literal reading)'

issues.problem: 'L-saturated convex sets of E (C + L ⊆ C: the open, the closed, the conical ones)' is true only of those CONTAINING L: an open ball of ℝ² not meeting L = {x = 0} is not L-saturated. Also, the subtype does not ask L ⊆ C, so the equivalence is saturated convex sets of E ↔ ALL convex sets of E/L. The 'containing L ↔ containing O' form, the exact analogue of convexQuotientEquiv, is a corollary that is not stated
issues.fix: Write '(C + L ⊆ C: e.g. the open, the closed or the conical convex sets containing L)' in both places, and add one sentence: 'no containment of L is asked; under the equivalence, C ⊇ L ⟺ O ∈ q(C)'
